rationale: K2 (M60 kotlin deep review, 2026-09-27): the five `uses` classes, and — the load-bearing half — every gate that SUPPRESSES one. 1,758 edges on the primary corpus came from five emission sites that no oracle derived, so nothing compared them. A fixture that pins only EMISSIONS cannot catch a rule that starts publishing too much, and that is the direction all three real defects went: the data-class certainty violation (bfad17e9), the init-block local given ownerName = its class (aa6a2beb), and the delegation-argument fabrication. Each of those publishes a NEW edge, so each is caught by a forbid here, not by an expect. Gate A (the member whitelist) and gate B (local bindings shadow members) do not cover for each other: gate B only walks function/lambda/ctor scopes, so a read in a class-level position — an init block, a superclass delegation — is caught by gate A or by nothing. The forbids for `scratch` and `argument` are that fact made permanent. `scratch` and `opening` are asserted as symbols WITHOUT an owner: a local IS a real symbol, it simply is not a member, and the M60 defect was in the owner field rather than in extraction — so pinning the kind alone would not have caught it. The forbids below do.

expectRelationships.note: QUALIFIED coroutine dispatcher: scope.async — the callee is a navigation_expression, not a bare identifier
indexing READ: the receiver's name, never the text `tags[0]`
chained index: the whole dotted SPINE survives, call parens and the trailing index do not
the chain base is also a bare member read — a distinct, legitimate edge
bare member read: the property read that used to publish nothing
string-template read: kotlin's grammar exposes a real interpolated_identifier
a constructor `val` IS a member and is readable from the body
a REAL member read inside an init block still publishes
an enum entry is a member (enum_class_body, not class_body)
enum entry, referenced from the body
enum entry, referenced from inside a method
a companion's members ARE the owner's: companion_object is not an object_declaration, so owner resolution walks past it to the class

forbidRelationships.note: an indexing WRITE is not a read: `=` and `op=` both parse as `assignment` whose first named child is the lhs, so the gate is by SPAN, never by text
gate B: a local bound in the function's scope shadows the member; without it `val seed = 99` fabricates a read of the property it shadows

an init-block LOCAL is not a member. THE M60 DEFECT (aa6a2beb): the walk carried the class down through `anonymous_initializer`, so this local was given ownerName = Counter and published this edge plus a phantom `contains`
the same wrong owner published a phantom containment — the java pass closed that shape as JD-J13

a constructor ARGUMENT is not a member. The delegation hangs off the class itself, so gate B's walk breaks at the class and can never reach a scope to find the name bound; only the val/var `binding_pattern_kind` makes a parameter a member
not a declared member of the enclosing type: gate A
